# 74120 - Pulse synchronizer

Package DIP-16 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/74120.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/74120.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 25 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![74120 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/74120.png) | ![74120 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-74120.png) | ![74120 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-74120.png) |

A rectangle for the whole function (or one section of it). Pin numbers are written on the lines where they meet the box; signal names are written beside them.

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 6,10 | Y = C AND PASS | While the section is passing pulses, Y carries the clock pulses of C (16 ns typical from C); the start/stop latch and the clock latch decide whether a pulse is passed, and a pulse once started is passed in full (latched, not clipped). Formula is the behaviour described in the text, not the gate-level wiring. |
| 7,9 | Y' = NOT Y | Complement of Y (9 ns typical from C). |

## Stored state

Bits stored: 2

Changes on: levels and high-to-low transitions on R, S1, S2; clock C

- R X, S1 L, S2 X: pass output pulses
- R X, S1 X, S2 L: pass output pulses
- R L, S1 H, S2 H: inhibit output pulses
- R H, S1 high-to-low, S2 H: start output pulses
- R H, S1 H, S2 high-to-low: start output pulses
- R high-to-low, S1 H, S2 H: stop output pulses
- R H, S1 H, S2 H: continue (operation started by the last high-to-low transition continues)
- After start, M low: pulses keep passing until a stop command; M high: only a single clock pulse is passed
- When stopped by S or R, the setup times decide which is the last pulse. A low-to-high transition on M meeting tsu(H) passes that positive clock pulse, then inhibits remaining pulses. Low-to-high transitions on M in the 20 ns after the falling edge of the clock pulse may or may not let the next pulse through.
- Once an output pulse has started it is not cut short (C is latch-controlled)

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 48 |
| outputHighMaxCurrentMa | -2.4 |
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | Clock driver: outputs drive 60 Series 54/74 loads high and 30 loads low. M, R and S inputs have internal pull-up resistors (15 kOhm nominal shown in the input schematic) and may be left open; the C input has none. C input low-level current -3.2 mA max, other inputs -2.1 mA max. |

## Propagation delays

All measured at VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, CL 45 pF, RL 133 ohm.

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | Y | PLH | 14 | 22 |
| C | Y | PHL | 17 | 25 |
| C | Y' | PLH | 10 | 16 |
| C | Y' | PHL | 8 | 13 |

## Timing limits

| What | Pin | Against | Min ns |
|---|---|---|---|
| setup | any input except M | C | 12 |
| setup | M | C | 0 |
| setup | M | C | 12 |
| hold | any input except M | C | 3 |
| hold | M | C | 20 |

## Not known

- Gate-level wiring: the datasheet gives none; the behaviour block models the function table and Figures 2-5.

## Notes

Typical power 127 mW per driver.
